newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco to float 20 pct of silver mine stake.
newsitem.headline: Morocco to float 20 pct of silver mine stake.

text.p: Morocco has decided to float 20 percent of its minority stake in the Imiter silver mine worth $13.7 million on the bourse next week, the privatisation ministry said on Tuesday.

"The flotation of (a stake) in Imiter firm worth 130.3 million dirhams ($13.7 million), or 396 dirhams per share, will take place on the Casablanca bourse next week," a privatisation ministry official said.
Subscription will be open to the general public from 9 to 13 June, 1997, he said.

He said it would be "the 12th flotation of the bourse" since the government launched its privatisation programme in 1993. The authorities plan to sell stakes in 113 firms, including banks and sugar plants by end 1998.

The state holds a stake of 33 percent of Societe Metallurgique d'Imiter (SMI) through the state-run Bureau des Recherches et Participations Minieres (BRPM), the remaining 67 percent of the capital is held by Morocco's largest private conglomerate ONA group.
Last year, ONA purchased four mines, including stakes in Imiter at more than 400 million dirhams, officials said.

One of the 10 profitable silver mines in the world with an estimated 1,000 grammes of silver per tonne of mineral products, Imiter has a life expectancy of up to eight years, Upline Securities stockbroker said.
The mine is located in the mountainous province of Ouarzazate, 500 kilometres south east of the Moroccan capital of Rabat.
Imiter had a turnover of 258.1 million dirhams in 1996, down from 309.8 million in 1995.
Morocco's silver output is estimated at 220 tonnes per year, of which Imiter holds 90 percent of total production, the privatisation ministry said.
Imiter is expected to be listed on the bourse on June 17, the ministry added.
